Our Story

Beirut · 2026

A kitchen.
A city.
A conversation.

How it started

Good Thing opened its doors with a simple conviction: that a great night out is built on more than food. It is built on people — on the energy of a room, the hands behind the plate, and the stories that travel with every ingredient. The restaurant quickly became a fixture in Beirut's social fabric, a place where chefs, writers, architects, and anyone who cares deeply about something tend to end up.

The Guest Chef Series was born out of that same conviction. We wanted to bring the world's most interesting chefs — not the most famous, but the most interesting — into our kitchen. To let them cook the way they cook at home, with the produce they know, for a room full of strangers who are about to become regulars.

The format

Each residency runs for four nights. The chef takes over the kitchen entirely. The menu is set — one sitting, one experience, no à la carte. Seats are limited, the room is intimate, and every evening is different from the last. When it is over, it is over. There are no reruns.

We have hosted chefs from Mexico, Peru, Spain — and in 2026 we are expanding the series across seven countries, each chef bringing a cuisine that has never been served in Beirut quite like this.

Why Beirut

Because Beirut understands hospitality at a cellular level. Because this city has always known how to sit with strangers, share a table, and make something beautiful out of very little. We chose to build this series here because nowhere else in the world would it land quite the same way.

A note from the founder

“Good Thing has always been about people as much as it is about food. The Guest Chef Series is our way of opening the kitchen to voices we admire — chefs who cook with intention, who carry a place and a story in every dish they put on the table.

Beirut deserves that. A city that has always known how to sit together, eat well, and make something out of nothing. We built this series for those evenings — the ones you don’t forget.

Welcome to our table.”
Omar Jheir
Founder, Good Thing
